title: Void Ending in a Conjunction with Jupiter
source: Picatrix (adapted), Book I chapter 5, Book II chapter 3 and Book III chapter 1

<!-- generated by tools/content/gen-void.ts; edit the generator, not this file -->

The conjunction is the closest bond the Moon makes: at it, her strength takes on the nature of the planet she has joined, and the doctrine of the fifth quality treats her meeting with the Sun as the strongest of all her figures. A course that closes on a conjunction ends in union rather than separation, the Moon's virtue soaked through with the planet's own nature.

When the Moon closes her course in a sign with a conjunction with Jupiter, the quiet stretch that follows carries something of his temperate growth. Jupiter is the Great Fortune, hot and humid and temperate, the source of growing power: law, legality, jurisprudence, wisdom, the interpretation of dreams, and the ready winning of requests. His benevolence fits clergymen, kings, and lords; tin is his metal, the emerald and every shining white stone are his, and his animals are the beautiful and harmless ones once used for sacrifice. Set in the ascendant or at mid-heaven, the text says, he rectifies the Moon's misfortunes.
